belief: If I don’t feel close to God, He has left me.
meta: A Christian look at the false belief that if you don’t feel close to God He has left you, with Scripture, questions, and homework for replacing it with the truth.
origins: Times of spiritual dryness after seasons of closeness. Depression or grief that dulls all feelings, including spiritual ones. Teaching that stressed feelings as proof of God’s presence. Sin or guilt that made you feel distant. Comparing your quiet faith with others’ emotional experiences.
teaches: God’s presence does not depend on your feelings. His Word promises, “He will never leave you nor forsake you.” There is nowhere you can go to escape His Spirit. Even the psalmists sometimes felt as though God had forgotten them and hidden His face, but they kept talking to Him. Feelings of distance are real and painful, but they are not a reliable report of where God is.
self_statements: I can’t feel Him, so He must be gone.
I must have done something to drive Him away.
Other people feel God, but I don’t.
My prayers just hit the ceiling.
God is close to others, not to me.
errors: Treating a feeling of distance as proof that God has left.
Assuming the dryness must be your fault.
Measuring God’s presence by other people’s feelings.
Predicting that you will always feel this way.
questions: What does God promise in Deuteronomy 31:8?
Where can I go that God is not, according to Psalm 139?
Did the psalmists ever feel forgotten? What did they do?
Could depression, grief, or exhaustion be affecting my feelings?
Is God’s presence based on His promise or my feelings?
Have I had dry times before that passed?
What would faithfulness look like during a dry season?
truth: Even when I don’t feel close to God, He has not left me. He promises never to leave me or forsake me. There is nowhere I can go to escape His presence. My feelings may be dry or numb, but God is still holding my hand. I can keep talking to Him and trust His promise.
hw_questions: What does God promise in Deuteronomy 31:8?
Where can I go that God is not?
What did the psalmists do when they felt forgotten?
Could depression or grief affect my feelings?
Is God’s presence based on promise or feeling?
hw_truths: God will never leave me nor forsake me.
I cannot go anywhere God is not.
My feelings are not a report of where God is.
God holds my right hand, even when I feel nothing.
I can keep talking to God in dry seasons.
God is the strength of my heart.
log: Each day, write: “God is with me today,” and one small sign of His care, even if I didn’t feel it.
name_example: The LORD Himself goes before Sarah; He will be with her. He will never leave her nor forsake her. She need not be afraid or discouraged.
actions: noticing how the writer moves from “How long?” to trust.

prayer: Father, I don’t feel close to You right now. Help me reject the lie that You have left me. Thank You that You will never leave me nor forsake me, and that I cannot go anywhere You are not. Hold my hand through this dry season and help me trust Your promise. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
